<section name="Conventions" source="repo" priority="1">
<document source="specs/collaborative-feature-planning/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="1.00" tokens="454">
## Integration & Relationships

- **Smart Feature Planning (`specs/7-feature-planning`, ADR-027/029).** This
  feature changes *how round feedback is authored*, not what a round is. The
  `user_answers` contract (FR-4.1/4.2), the `feature_review` human station and its
  accept / refine / abandon outcomes (FR-4.7), the single-round-in-flight rule
  (FR-4.5) and the single-finalize rule (FR-12.11) all stand. The planning line
  (`analyze → author → …`) is unchanged; the `author` wait node is simply resumed
  by whichever collaborator acts.
- **Web-UI auth (`apps/web-ui/src/lib/session.ts`, `user-repo-access.ts`).** The
  GitHub session already identifies the viewer, and `userCanAccessRepo` already
  answers "may this person see this repo". Collaboration reuses both; it adds no
  new identity provider or invitation system.
- **SSE run observability (ADR-037).** ADR-037 introduced the stack's only
  streaming transport, one-way, carried by an in-process pub/sub that is sound
  only under a pinned single replica. Live co-editing needs a **bidirectional**
  channel and durable document state, which ADR-037 does not provide. The
  transport, merge algorithm and persistence are decided in a new ADR (see
  Open Decisions) *before* implementation, per the ADR-before-implementation
  practice. The single-replica constraint (`lore-api-helm` `replicaCount: 1`)
  applies to it the same way and must be named, not assumed away.
- **Project facade & ports (ADR-024).** Shared feedback documents and
  contributor attribution are persisted behind the existing `features` port on
  the Project object, alongside iterations.
- **Planning prompt (`scripts/task-types.yaml`, FR-2.3/2.6).** The composed
  timeline gains authorship on each prior comment and answer. The prompt is still
  the yaml template verbatim.
</document>
<document source="specs/assembly-line-run-viz/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="0.54" tokens="1104" truncated="true">
## Retired Requirements (Background)

- FR2.7 _(retired 2026-09-23)_: the `Cache-Control`, `X-Accel-Buffering` and identity-encoding response headers. Removed: they protected an HTTP response from buffering intermediaries, and a WebSocket frame has no such hop.
- FR4.8 _(retired 2026-09-23)_: the proxy hop's repeated stream headers. Removed with the SSE proxy; see FR4.7a.

- FR5.8 _(retired 2026-09-09)_: the 10-second `router.refresh()` of the server-rendered half while a run was live. Removed: the header, the node rows and the task events now change in place from the multiplexed stream (FR7.8–FR7.10). The retired statement read:
  - FR5.8. _(added 2026-09-02)_ A live run's page keeps up with the SERVER-RENDERED half of itself. The SSE stream carries agent events, deliberately not node state (ADR-037; node state seeds from `pipeline.station_runs`), so the header status, the panel's seed node rows and a recorded outcome only changed on a manual reload. While the run is non-terminal the page re-runs its server component on a 10s cadence (`router.refresh()` — client state, the stream and the selection survive it); a terminal run refreshes nothing, because its snapshot is the truth and an idle page must not poll forever.
- FR4.4i, FR4.6b–d _(retired 2026-09-09)_: the run Timeline card (lifecycle ticks on a wall-clock rail) and the replay scrubber (terminal-run fold to a cursor, the pure slider control, and tick-to-cursor seeking). Removed: the timeline restated what the graph and the transcript already show, and the scrubber's replay plumbing was most of the panel's complexity for a control nobody reached for. `replayTo` and the reducer's replayable-from-zero property stay (FR4.6a); `RunTimelineView`, `ReplayScrubberView`, `run-timeline`, `replayRunData`, `completedRowsAt`, `cursorForEventId`, `scrubberPositionLabel` and the reducer's `timeline` accumulator were deleted with their tests. The retired statements read:
  - FR4.4i. Each lifecycle tick is placed at its wall-clock fraction of the run's span, whose right bound is the live run's moving `now`, and is coloured by event type, so a node whose latest tick lags far behind the now edge reads as stalled; a run with no ticks renders an explicit empty state rather than a bare rail, and the whole strip renders as a collapsible card titled Timeline.
  - FR4.6b. The replay scrubber renders only for a terminal run and folds that run's persisted history through the same reducer to a chosen cursor, so the graph, transcript, heatmap, and timeline all render the state as of that event; a live run keeps streaming and shows no scrubber, and a Back to live control clears the cursor to restore the final state. The reducer is therefore replayable-from-zero — folding from the all-idle base to cursor N, advancing past it, and rewinding to N yields byte-identical state — which is the only reason a node's status and iteration rewind rather than only advance. The taken-path overlay and the verdict badges derive from the events applied up to the cursor as well: a walk row's recorded verdict becomes visible only once the replay has applied that node-iteration's `result` event — the verdict's value still comes only from the row, never from the event itself — the max-iteration completed row wins regardless of row order, an executed node the cursor has not reached disappears from run mode, and no terminal result badge shows mid-replay; the cursor's right end renders byte-identically to Back to live.
  - FR4.6c. The scrubber is a pure control that reports a cursor and nothing else: a range slider over the event count, keyboard stepping that steps one event on left/right and jumps to the first event on Home and the latest on End while clamping at both ends, and a position read-out that names the moment as `event N / M` plus the last applied event's wall-clock time rather than a bare index.
  - FR4.6d. A timeline tick seeks the scrubber to the cursor that includes that tick's event, so the timeline is the coarse navigator and the slider the fine one; an id that matches no event leaves the cursor unchanged.
- FR4.4g _(retired 2026-09-02)_: the dedicated transcript scroll viewport — follow-the-tail auto-scroll and per-node scroll-offset memory in a bounded scroll box. Removed: the transcript now renders in the page's own flow, and the scroll helpers, their tests, and the panel's scroll wiring were deleted with it.
</document>

/** Follows the plan's run on the tab's live socket, with no `router.refresh()`. A seed the server re-rendered with (Approve, Regenerate, …) outranks whatever the socket folded in from the run it already reflects, so a changed seed resets the fold. */
export function usePlanRunLive(
  seed: PlanRun | null,
  refreshRunFacts: PlanActions["refreshRunFacts"],
): PlanRun | null {
  const [live, dispatch] = useReducer(reducePlanRunLive, seed, (run) =>
    initialPlanRunLive(run ?? EMPTY_RUN_FACTS, run?.nodes ?? []),
  );
  const [facts, setFacts] = useState(seed);

  useEffect(() => adoptSeed(seed, dispatch, setFacts), [seed, dispatch]);
  const scheduleFactsRefresh = useDebouncedCallback(
    () => void refreshFacts(refreshRunFacts, setFacts),
    SETTLE_MS,
  );

  useRunChannel(channelOptions(seed, dispatch, scheduleFactsRefresh));

  return facts && { ...facts, ...live.run, nodes: live.nodes };
}

function openPlan(
  latest: LatestPlan,
  client: LiveSocketClient | null,
  setConnection: (connection: Connection) => void,
) {
  let closed = false;
  const opening = connectPlan(
    latest.current.meta,
    () => latest.current.openSocket(),
    client,
  );

  void opening.then((opened) => !closed && setConnection(opened));

  return () => {
    closed = true;
    void opening.then(
      (opened) => "transport" in opened && opened.transport.destroy(),
    );
  };
}
</document>

function registerLiveSocket(
  server: Hapi.Server,
  getPool: () => Pool | null,
  collab: RegisteredPlanning["collab"],

<document source="adrs/ADR-048-one-websocket-for-live-channels.md" type="adr" relevance="1.00" tokens="871">
## Consequences

- The SSE route `GET /api/assembly-runs/{id}/stream`, the web-ui's session-authenticated SSE proxy and the `EventSource` hook are deleted. The browser reaches lore-api's socket directly at its public host, as the plan editor already did; the web-ui nginx ingress and its 60-second read timeout are no longer on the path.
- The run stream's contract, cursor semantics and Postgres `NOTIFY` fan-out are unchanged; ADR-037's amendments on those points stand. What changed is who listens: one feed per run instead of one session per connection, so a run with N viewers costs one re-read per notification instead of N.
- `LORE_PLANS_WS_URL` becomes `LORE_WS_URL` (`wss://<lore-api host>/api/ws`). Terraform sets it; CI never runs terraform, so the apply must land with the deploy.
- lore-api still runs one replica while plans are live (ADR-047). The run channel is fan-out-safe across replicas, but both channels share one socket, so scaling lore-api needs sticky routing for the socket, not only for plans. No planning-station change was needed for this: the library's `/api/plans/collab` mount stays on the listener, and lore-api tunnels to the same Hocuspocus instance the planning registration returns.
- The plan and run channels live in one feature folder, `apps/lore-api/src/work/assembly-line-station/`, together with the run stream's frames, session reads and notification hub.

title: "One WebSocket carries the browser's live channels"
status: accepted

# ADR-048: One WebSocket carries the browser's live channels

This ADR replaces the run page's Server-Sent Events stream with one WebSocket per browser tab, served by lore-api at `/api/ws`, that multiplexes named channels: a `run` channel forwards an assembly run's pod events and transcript to everyone registered for that run, and a `plan` channel tunnels the plan editor's collaboration protocol, so a navigation from a plan to its run keeps the connection.

## Decision

### One socket, many channels

- lore-api serves one WebSocket upgrade at `/api/ws` on its own listener, beside the plans library's mount, and leaves any other upgrade path to the mount that owns it.
- Every message is one JSON text frame with a client-chosen channel id. A client opens a channel with `open` (kind `run`, `runs` or `plan`), closes it with `close`, and sends a plan channel's bytes as base64 with `send`; the server answers `opened`, `frame`, `data`, `closed` with a reason, or `error` with a code. The contract is published in OpenAPI as `LiveClientMessage` and `LiveServerMessage` beside `RunStreamFrame`, with the socket named by a root `x-websocket` extension, so the web-ui reads generated types.
- A message that is not JSON, names an unknown type, opens a run without a token, or carries a non-numeric cursor is refused as `bad_message`; a channel id already open is `channel_in_use`; a ninth channel on one socket is `too_many_channels`; an open past the socket's rate limit is `rate_limited`; a send or close for a channel the socket does not hold is `unknown_channel`. None of them takes the socket down.
- The socket pings every 25 seconds and terminates a peer that misses a pong; a socket that goes closes every channel it held, once, and a channel a handler ended itself is forgotten without closing it again.

adr_number: 37
title: "SSE for assembly-line run observability"
status: superseded
date: 2026-07-17
domains: [architecture, observability, floor, web-ui]

# ADR-037: SSE for assembly-line run observability

This ADR adopts Server-Sent Events as the transport for live assembly-line run observability — the stack's first streaming transport — carried by an in-process pub/sub that is sound only under the Floor's pinned single replica, with PG LISTEN/NOTIFY named as the multi-replica escape hatch behind an unchanged subscribe API.

> **Superseded (2026-09-23) by [ADR-048](ADR-048-one-websocket-for-live-channels.md).** The transport is now one WebSocket per browser tab that multiplexes a `run` channel and a `plan` channel. The frame contract, the row-id cursor, the catch-up-then-live semantics and the Postgres fan-out this ADR and its amendments settled are unchanged and are what ADR-048 builds on; the SSE route, the `EventSource` hook and the web-ui proxy hop are gone, and the "WebSocket" entry under Alternatives below no longer holds now that the plan editor had already paid for one. The links in the Decision and the 2026-09-09 amendment point at the tests as they are today, under the live socket.

## Alternatives

**Read the existing GCS raw-NDJSON archive instead of projecting a table.**
Rejected. The archive is keyed by ingest timestamp rather than by run, has no
cursor, and cannot be tailed — it
supports post-hoc replay of a blob, not a live view or a resumable stream.
Serving a run page from it would mean fetching and parsing whole NDJSON objects
per view. It remained valuable as a raw audit substrate until
`pipeline.agent_run_turns` subsumed that role, and was retired then (see the
amendment in Context, #1148).

**WebSocket.** Rejected. The traffic is unidirectional server-to-client; a
WebSocket buys a full duplex channel nothing needs, in exchange for a protocol
upgrade through the ingress, a heartbeat/reconnect state machine written by hand,
and a client library or hand-rolled equivalent. SSE gets automatic browser
reconnection and `Last-Event-ID` resumption for free, which is precisely the
catch-up-then-live semantic the spec requires. Native `EventSource` needs no
dependency.

**Polling, as every other live view does.** Rejected for this view specifically.
A per-tool-call transcript at a 4–15 second poll interval renders as jumps rather
than as a stream, and closing the interval enough to feel live turns each viewer
into a repeated whole-window query. The existing polled views stay polled.

**A third-party SSE or realtime library.** Rejected. SSE framing is a handful of
lines of text, `EventSource` is native, and this epic is explicitly zero-dep.

**A `node_status` event type published alongside the run events.** Rejected. Node
state already has a source of truth in `pipeline.station_runs`, which the
walk writes; a parallel status event would be a second source that drifts against
it. The client seeds from the table and derives running-versus-finished from the
per-node `init` and `result` events.

**An off-the-shelf graph layout library for the DAG.** Rejected. Every assembly
line definition in `libs/assembly-lines/src/assembly-lines/*.yaml` is at most 7
nodes today — `implementation.yaml` is the largest at exactly 7 (implement,
validate, push, review, address, retrospective, done), including an
`implement → implement` self-loop and the `validate → implement` and
`address → validate` back-edges, so the renderer must handle cycles but not
scale. At that size a hand-rolled layered SVG layout is smaller than the adapter
code a library would need. This is an observed bound, not one the layout
enforces; a definition substantially larger than that is the trigger to revisit,
and the fallback is a layout dependency confined to the renderer, not a change to
the transport or the contract.
</document>

**session-summary/2026-09-23-one-live-socket** (memory): Replaced the run page's SSE stream with ONE WebSocket per browser tab (branch feat/one-live-socket, ADR-048). lore-api mounts an upgrade at /api/ws on its own listener beside planning-sync's /api/plans/collab mount; JSON text frames with client-chosen channel ids: `run` channel (token minted by POST /api/assembly-runs/{id}/stream-token, lore.live_tokens migration 0091, sha256 + 10-min TTL like plan collab tokens) and `plan` channel (tunnels Hocuspocus bytes to `sync.collab.handleConnection(duck, webRequest)` — Hocuspocus only touches readyState/send/close on the socket; the collab-token handshake stays inside the tunnel, so NO planning-station change). Server side: one feed per run (apps/lore-api/src/work/assembly-line-station/run-feed.ts) subscribes once to the hub and re-reads once per notification, forwarding to every registered viewer; catch-up per viewer on the feed's chain (no queue needed because catch-up and live reads serialize on one chain). Everything moved into work/assembly-line-station/ (user demanded one dedicated folder). Web-ui: LiveSocketProvider in root layout, pure connection-machine reducer + client IO shell, useRunChannel replaces useRunEventStream (task page too), channel-websocket.ts = Hocuspocus WebSocketPolyfill built with `transportFor` from @re-cinq/planning-editor and a direct @hocuspocus/provider dep. LORE_PLANS_WS_URL → LORE_WS_URL in terraform (needs apply). GOTCHAS: (1) zod4 discriminatedUnion cannot repeat `type:"open"` with different `kind` — use z.union. (2) Hocuspocus 4.7 sends PermissionDenied but does NOT close the socket after a refused token; the provider closes itself. (3) An authenticated plan channel keeps emitting sync frames, so integration tests must filter replies by channel. (4) In jsdom tests acknowledging the run channel flips the task page to the heartbeat poll cadence; tests that expect the coordinated poll must accept the socket without answering `opened`. (5) reanchor.mjs cannot map links into NEW test files (no base copy) — run prettier BEFORE writing links, or re-resolve by test title from the eslint require-spec-link listing. (6) check-openapi-drift.sh diffs against HEAD, so it "fails" on an uncommitted regeneration; trust gen-openapi.test. (7) the "use server" action imported by a client hook drags `server-only` into jsdom suites — mock the action module. (8) Two `upgrade` listeners share hapi's listener; each must ignore foreign paths and never destroy the socket.

**session-summary/2026-09-23-one-live-socket** (fact) [inferred]: A WebSocket implementation replaced the run page's SSE stream, with one WebSocket per browser tab in branch feat/one-live-socket (ADR-048).

/** Follows the plan's run on the tab's live socket, with no `router.refresh()`. A seed the server re-rendered with (Approve, Regenerate, …) outranks whatever the socket folded in from the run it already reflects, so a changed seed resets the fold. */
export function usePlanRunLive(
  seed: PlanRun | null,
  refreshRunFacts: PlanActions["refreshRunFacts"],
): PlanRun | null {
  const [live, dispatch] = useReducer(reducePlanRunLive, seed, (run) =>
    initialPlanRunLive(run ?? EMPTY_RUN_FACTS, run?.nodes ?? []),
  );
  const [facts, setFacts] = useState(seed);

  useEffect(() => adoptSeed(seed, dispatch, setFacts), [seed, dispatch]);
  const scheduleFactsRefresh = useDebouncedCallback(
    () => void refreshFacts(refreshRunFacts, setFacts),
    SETTLE_MS,
  );

  useRunChannel(channelOptions(seed, dispatch, scheduleFactsRefresh));

  return facts && { ...facts, ...live.run, nodes: live.nodes };
}

function openPlan(
  latest: LatestPlan,
  client: LiveSocketClient | null,
  setConnection: (connection: Connection) => void,
) {
  let closed = false;
  const opening = connectPlan(
    latest.current.meta,
    () => latest.current.openSocket(),
    client,
  );

  void opening.then((opened) => !closed && setConnection(opened));

  return () => {
    closed = true;
    void opening.then(
      (opened) => "transport" in opened && opened.transport.destroy(),
    );
  };
}

## Consequences

- The SSE route `GET /api/assembly-runs/{id}/stream`, the web-ui's session-authenticated SSE proxy and the `EventSource` hook are deleted. The browser reaches lore-api's socket directly at its public host, as the plan editor already did; the web-ui nginx ingress and its 60-second read timeout are no longer on the path.
- The run stream's contract, cursor semantics and Postgres `NOTIFY` fan-out are unchanged; ADR-037's amendments on those points stand. What changed is who listens: one feed per run instead of one session per connection, so a run with N viewers costs one re-read per notification instead of N.
- `LORE_PLANS_WS_URL` becomes `LORE_WS_URL` (`wss://<lore-api host>/api/ws`). Terraform sets it; CI never runs terraform, so the apply must land with the deploy.
- lore-api still runs one replica while plans are live (ADR-047). The run channel is fan-out-safe across replicas, but both channels share one socket, so scaling lore-api needs sticky routing for the socket, not only for plans. No planning-station change was needed for this: the library's `/api/plans/collab` mount stays on the listener, and lore-api tunnels to the same Hocuspocus instance the planning registration returns.
- The plan and run channels live in one feature folder, `apps/lore-api/src/work/assembly-line-station/`, together with the run stream's frames, session reads and notification hub.

# ADR-048: One WebSocket carries the browser's live channels

This ADR replaces the run page's Server-Sent Events stream with one WebSocket per browser tab, served by lore-api at `/api/ws`, that multiplexes named channels: a `run` channel forwards an assembly run's pod events and transcript to everyone registered for that run, and a `plan` channel tunnels the plan editor's collaboration protocol, so a navigation from a plan to its run keeps the connection.

## Decision

### One socket, many channels

- lore-api serves one WebSocket upgrade at `/api/ws` on its own listener, beside the plans library's mount, and leaves any other upgrade path to the mount that owns it.
- Every message is one JSON text frame with a client-chosen channel id. A client opens a channel with `open` (kind `run`, `runs` or `plan`), closes it with `close`, and sends a plan channel's bytes as base64 with `send`; the server answers `opened`, `frame`, `data`, `closed` with a reason, or `error` with a code. The contract is published in OpenAPI as `LiveClientMessage` and `LiveServerMessage` beside `RunStreamFrame`, with the socket named by a root `x-websocket` extension, so the web-ui reads generated types.
- A message that is not JSON, names an unknown type, opens a run without a token, or carries a non-numeric cursor is refused as `bad_message`; a channel id already open is `channel_in_use`; a ninth channel on one socket is `too_many_channels`; an open past the socket's rate limit is `rate_limited`; a send or close for a channel the socket does not hold is `unknown_channel`. None of them takes the socket down.
- The socket pings every 25 seconds and terminates a peer that misses a pong; a socket that goes closes every channel it held, once, and a channel a handler ended itself is forgotten without closing it again.

# ADR-037: SSE for assembly-line run observability

This ADR adopts Server-Sent Events as the transport for live assembly-line run observability — the stack's first streaming transport — carried by an in-process pub/sub that is sound only under the Floor's pinned single replica, with PG LISTEN/NOTIFY named as the multi-replica escape hatch behind an unchanged subscribe API.

> **Superseded (2026-09-23) by [ADR-048](ADR-048-one-websocket-for-live-channels.md).** The transport is now one WebSocket per browser tab that multiplexes a `run` channel and a `plan` channel. The frame contract, the row-id cursor, the catch-up-then-live semantics and the Postgres fan-out this ADR and its amendments settled are unchanged and are what ADR-048 builds on; the SSE route, the `EventSource` hook and the web-ui proxy hop are gone, and the "WebSocket" entry under Alternatives below no longer holds now that the plan editor had already paid for one. The links in the Decision and the 2026-09-09 amendment point at the tests as they are today, under the live socket.

## Alternatives

**Read the existing GCS raw-NDJSON archive instead of projecting a table.**
Rejected. The archive is keyed by ingest timestamp rather than by run, has no
cursor, and cannot be tailed — it
supports post-hoc replay of a blob, not a live view or a resumable stream.
Serving a run page from it would mean fetching and parsing whole NDJSON objects
per view. It remained valuable as a raw audit substrate until
`pipeline.agent_run_turns` subsumed that role, and was retired then (see the
amendment in Context, #1148).

**WebSocket.** Rejected. The traffic is unidirectional server-to-client; a
WebSocket buys a full duplex channel nothing needs, in exchange for a protocol
upgrade through the ingress, a heartbeat/reconnect state machine written by hand,
and a client library or hand-rolled equivalent. SSE gets automatic browser
reconnection and `Last-Event-ID` resumption for free, which is precisely the
catch-up-then-live semantic the spec requires. Native `EventSource` needs no
dependency.

**Polling, as every other live view does.** Rejected for this view specifically.
A per-tool-call transcript at a 4–15 second poll interval renders as jumps rather
than as a stream, and closing the interval enough to feel live turns each viewer
into a repeated whole-window query. The existing polled views stay polled.

**A third-party SSE or realtime library.** Rejected. SSE framing is a handful of
lines of text, `EventSource` is native, and this epic is explicitly zero-dep.

**A `node_status` event type published alongside the run events.** Rejected. Node
state already has a source of truth in `pipeline.station_runs`, which the
walk writes; a parallel status event would be a second source that drifts against
it. The client seeds from the table and derives running-versus-finished from the
per-node `init` and `result` events.

**An off-the-shelf graph layout library for the DAG.** Rejected. Every assembly
line definition in `libs/assembly-lines/src/assembly-lines/*.yaml` is at most 7
nodes today — `implementation.yaml` is the largest at exactly 7 (implement,
validate, push, review, address, retrospective, done), including an
`implement → implement` self-loop and the `validate → implement` and
`address → validate` back-edges, so the renderer must handle cycles but not
scale. At that size a hand-rolled layered SVG layout is smaller than the adapter
code a library would need. This is an observed bound, not one the layout
enforces; a definition substantially larger than that is the trigger to revisit,
and the fallback is a layout dependency confined to the renderer, not a change to
the transport or the contract.
</document>
